title: Tteokbokki
subtitle: korean spicy rice cakes
excerpt: Tteokbokki is a Korean street food dish of cylindrical rice cakes simmered in a sweet and spicy sauce made from gochujang and soy sauce. It is chewy, sticky, and intensely flavoured. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Tteokbokki is one of the most popular Korean street foods. The spicy version with gochujang sauce became the standard from the 1950s onwards, replacing an older royal court version made with soy sauce and beef.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce can be made a day ahead. Add the rice cakes when ready to serve.

glossaryTerms.definition: Korean rice cakes made from glutinous rice flour. Cylindrical tteok are used for tteokbokki. They are chewy, dense, and absorb sauce well.
A Korean fermented red chilli paste made from chilli powder, glutinous rice, and fermented soybeans. It is thick, spicy, and slightly sweet.

content.text: rice cakes that soak up the
sauce as they simmer. The result is chewy, coated, and very satisfying. Serves 4 as a snack or 2 as a main.
Frozen rice cakes work just as well as fresh ones. Soak them in cold water for 30 minutes before cooking to soften them and prevent cracking.

items.prepNote: or soy sauce to keep vegan

content.text: If using frozen rice cakes, soak in cold water for 30 minutes and drain. Separate any that are stuck together.
Mix the gochujang, soy sauce, fish sauce (or extra soy sauce), sugar, and garlic with 100 ml of the water to make a smooth sauce paste.
Pour the remaining water into a large saucepan and bring to a boil. Add the sauce paste and stir to combine. Add the sliced onion.
Add the rice cakes. Simmer over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring frequently, until the rice cakes are tender and the sauce has thickened and coats them well.
Add the spring onion in the last 2 minutes of cooking. Drizzle sesame oil over the top, scatter sesame seeds, and serve immediately. The sauce thickens further as it cools, so serve straight away.

attrs.issue: Rice cakes are still hard in the centre
attrs.fix: They need more time. Add a splash more water and simmer for a further 5 minutes. Frozen cakes may take longer than fresh ones.

attrs.issue: Sauce is too thick and catching on the bottom
attrs.fix: Add water 50 ml at a time, stirring constantly. Tteokbokki sauce thickens fast. Keep the heat at a medium simmer.
Reduce the gochujang to 2 tablespoons and add 1 extra teaspoon of sugar to balance. A spoonful of ketchup also cuts the heat without tasting out of place.

content.text: Tteokbokki is sold at pojangmacha food stalls across Korea. It is eaten standing up, in a paper cup, or at small outdoor tables. It is the defining Korean street food and especially popular with school children and students. Home versions are common and easy to make. Many Koreans add fish cake slices and boiled eggs to the pot as well.
